title: CI helm render checks: assert non-deployment templates with -s templates/<file>, pairing a default render with a --set override
answers: How do I add a CI check that the Service or CronJob in the Helm chart renders the right port?
How do I test a single Helm template in the GitHub workflow without rendering the whole chart?
Where are the chart render assertions for service.port defined?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/helm.yml runs the chart render checks; the `Render Service port` and `Render CronJob with a decoupled Service port` steps each define a local `render()` helper that runs `helm template mlflow charts/` with a dummy `mlflow.backendStoreUri` and then `-s templates/<file>.yaml` to select one template.
Rule: To check a value in a template other than deployment.yaml, select it with `-s templates/service.yaml` (or `cronjob.yaml`) in the render helper, and pass the override through "$@". Write the default case and the override case as a pair: `render | grep -q '<default line>'` then `render --set <key>=<value> | grep -q '<override line>'`. Use anchored greps on the exact rendered line (for example `'^    - port: 80$'`) or on a full value such as the in-cluster URL `mlflow.default.svc.cluster.local:80`.
Constraints: Add `--set fullnameOverride=mlflow` when the expected string depends on the release name, as the CronJob step does. The anchored indentation patterns depend on the template's nindent levels; update them if the template changes. Because `grep -q` runs inside a plain `run:` step, a missing line fails the step only if the grep fails, so keep one assertion per line.
applies: Changes to Helm chart render behaviour in charts/ for Service, CronJob or other non-deployment templates; adding CI render assertions in .github/workflows/helm.yml.
says: The deployed service does not expose the custom port configured during installation.
Scheduled background jobs cannot reach the tracking server cluster address after port changes.
Allow users to override the network port when installing the Kubernetes package.
Scheduled tasks fail to communicate with the service under a custom release name.
The internal cluster service ignores custom port values and uses default settings.
search: CI Helm chart render checks in .github/workflows/helm.yml test non-deployment templates by running helm template with -s templates/<file>.yaml, pairing default renders with --set overrides verified by anchored grep. Steps define a render helper with a dummy mlflow.backendStoreUri and pass overrides through $@, asserting exact rendered lines or in-cluster URLs. Add --set fullnameOverride=mlflow if expected strings depend on release names, update indentation patterns when nindent changes, and keep one assertion per run step. Applies to changes in charts/ for Service, CronJob, or other non-deployment templates and render assertions in .github/workflows/helm.yml.
